target: 100% completion of the selected original PlayStation 2 route, including preserved online features, spoiler-free

areas.name: Selected Route, Training, and Preserved Online
areas.location_cue: The PS2 title screen, Training Ground, memory-card interface, Network Play, and a private lobby.
areas.note: Establish a clean, reproducible original-release route before collecting anything.

levels.1: One console release contains the complete selected route.
levels.2: Use an original File #2 disc on a PlayStation 2 or a tested PS2 emulator.
levels.3: Confirm the disc region, controller, real-time menu, memory-card slot, and save operation before measuring progress. There is no secondary or definitive edition to merge.

items.label: Begin on a Clean Memory Card

levels.1: Imported data can make rewards appear before their requirements are met.
levels.2: Create a blank File #2 save and retain an untouched copy.
levels.3: Boot the chosen disc with a new card, verify the Collection and Scenario Select pages contain only initial entries, then clone the card. Keep separate working copies for difficulties, event marks, SP items, online play, and shop purchases.

levels.1: The practice route teaches systems added for this entry.
levels.2: Choose Training Ground and follow every on-screen lesson through its exit.
levels.3: Read each prompt, exchange an item with the AI partner, command that partner to use an item, help the downed partner stand, recover an item from another inventory, break the blocked door, and reach the tutorial finish.

levels.1: Community-hosted multiplayer depends on one regional build.
levels.2: Use a lawfully owned Japanese disc with the current OBSRV connection instructions.
levels.3: Dump your own Japanese disc and console firmware, preserve untouched hashes, then configure either native PS2 networking or a compatible PCSX2 build. Apply an optional translation patch only to a duplicate image.

levels.1: The retired official network has a maintained archival replacement.
levels.2: Register with OBSRV, use its current network values, and enter a private lobby.
levels.3: Follow OBSRV's live setup page because addresses may change. Create a separate account, test DNS and memory-card persistence, enter Network Play, create a passworded room, and reconnect once after a cold boot.

levels.1: Full cooperation exposes interactions that solo partners cannot demonstrate reliably.
levels.2: Clear any scenario with four human players connected from start to result screen.
levels.3: Use a private group, divide inventory and key-item duties, exchange one object, raise an injured teammate, respond with the built-in call system, and keep all four clients connected until the clear is recorded.

levels.1: A failed online survivor can briefly remain interactive.
levels.2: On a disposable private-room save, allow one consenting player's virus gauge to fill.
levels.3: Remove rare items, leave at least one teammate active, let the chosen gauge reach its limit, and record the temporary player-controlled hostile state. End the test, discard the altered card, and restore the clean online copy.

save_backup.title: Preserve the baseline
save_backup.why: Imported or pre-unlocked cards invalidate progression evidence.

areas.name: Final 100% Audit
areas.location_cue: Scenario records, event percentages, SP logs, Collection pages, online evidence, and memory-card copies.
areas.note: Do not declare completion until every independent total agrees.

levels.1: Five scenario pools and eight survivor pools form one hidden-object total.
levels.2: Verify 100 scenario-wide SP objects and 160 survivor-specific SP objects.
levels.3: Check every SP page: each main scenario must show twenty objects, and each of the eight survivors must show twenty. The combined count must be 260; this also exposes the final color-themed NPC group.

items.label: Reach 100% on All Five Event Lists

levels.1: Mutually exclusive triggers accumulate over many successful exits.
levels.2: Raise every scenario's event checklist to 100%.
levels.3: Compare the five numbered ledgers in this pack against the game after every result screen. Verify 100% separately for End of the Road and Flashback, then for Wild Things, Desperate Times, and Underbelly.

levels.1: Each difficulty changes resources and SP placement.
levels.2: Record twenty main clears: five scenarios on Easy, Normal, Hard, and Very Hard.
levels.3: Maintain a five-by-four grid outside the game, fill one cell only after its result saves, and keep Infinity disabled. Confirm every cell plus all eleven Extra-mode purchase and clear records.

levels.1: Character-linked art and costumes require broad scenario coverage.
levels.2: Clear all five scenarios with each of the eight main survivors.
levels.3: Track Kevin, Mark, Jim, George, David, Alyssa, Yoko, and Cindy against all five scenarios. Every one of the forty cells must have a saved result; use this clean matrix instead of importing File #1 completion data.

levels.1: The final archive spans images, costumes, movies, sounds, and extra modes.
levels.2: Buy 145 Gallery, 59 Costume, 146 Movie, 14 Sound, and 11 Extra entries.
levels.3: Count purchased markers by page and confirm 145 + 59 + 146 + 14 + 11 = 375. Open every gallery image and movie, preview every costume, play every sound, and launch every Extra option at least once.

levels.1: A clean final artifact should prove its own unlock route.
levels.2: Capture all event, SP, difficulty, survivor, Collection, and online summary pages.
levels.3: Cold-boot the original disc with the completed card, verify every total, clone the card twice, hash all three copies, and write-protect one archive. Keep the OBSRV profile and unmodified disc image beside, but separate from, the completion save.
